definitions.explanation: The rhythmic pattern or beat in music. Also used more broadly for timing or tempo.
Used in the pattern ～た{拍子|ひょうし}に to mean 'at the moment when' or 'just as (something happened)'.

examples.japanese: {三拍子|さんびょうし}のリズムで{踊|おど}る。
{手拍子|てびょうし}に{合|あ}わせて{歌|うた}った。
examples.english: I sang along to the hand clapping.

examples.japanese: {拍子|ひょうし}がずれているよ。
{立|た}ち{上|あ}がった{拍子|ひょうし}に{頭|あたま}をぶつけた。
examples.english: I bumped my head just as I stood up.

examples.japanese: くしゃみをした{拍子|ひょうし}に{腰|こし}を{痛|いた}めた。
examples.english: I hurt my back at the moment I sneezed.

examples.japanese: ドアを{開|あ}けた{拍子|ひょうし}に{風|かぜ}で{紙|かみ}が{飛|と}んでいった。
examples.english: Just as I opened the door, the papers blew away in the wind.

notes:
{拍子|ひょうし} has both a musical meaning (rhythm/beat) and a temporal meaning (the moment when something happens).

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {三拍子|さんびょうし}: triple time; also used in {三拍子|さんびょうし}{揃|そろ}う (to have all three desirable qualities)
- {手拍子|てびょうし}: hand clapping to a rhythm
- {拍子抜|ひょうしぬ}け: anticlimax, letdown

PATTERN:
- ～た{拍子|ひょうし}に: at the moment when, just as
  This pattern describes something unexpected happening simultaneously with an action.
